overview.summary: France has state-regulated fees at public universities, respected business and engineering schools, and a growing number of English-taught master’s programmes. Most bachelor’s programmes are taught in French.
overview.educationSystem: Public universities follow the LMD structure: licence (bachelor’s, 3 years), master (2 years) and doctorat. Grandes écoles and business schools are selective and often charge higher fees.

conditions: Up to 964 hours per year (about 60% of full-time work) without a separate work permit.
Your employer must declare you to the prefecture before you start.
Exceeding the limit can lead to withdrawal of your residence permit.
Most part-time jobs need conversational French. Earnings are not guaranteed.

postStudyRoutes.conditions: For graduates with at least a master’s-level degree (or a licence professionnelle) from France, to look for work or start a business.

postStudyRoutes.name: Talent passport or salaried worker permit
postStudyRoutes.conditions: Requires a qualifying job offer; salary thresholds apply for some permits.

lifestyle.text: CROUS student residences are cheapest but limited. Many students rent privately and may qualify for CAF housing assistance.
Excellent trains and urban transport with student discounts.
Varies from mild Mediterranean in the south to cooler, wetter weather in the north.
Register with French social security (sécurité sociale étudiante) after arrival; a complementary mutuelle is optional but common.
Generally safe. Watch for pickpockets in big cities.
